groups.when: Work with your Ouro agent from a coding tool: talk to it, hand it work, report back, and read its state.
Install, start, stop, update or inspect the Ouro runtime itself on this machine, and find commands.
Choose, credential and test the model providers each agent lane thinks with, and connect integrations.
Unlock, inspect and change the encrypted store holding an agent's secrets and machine config.
Manage the people an agent knows, their trust and linked accounts, and its live conversations.
Look inside an agent: its private runtime turns and state, attention queue, work board, and wake it.
Reach, import and maintain an agent's email: browser address, MBOX imports, index rebuilds, cleanup.
Connect coding tools to agents: MCP servers they serve or call, editor hooks and plugins.
Let an agent work with other agents: publish its card, onboard peers, message them, and grant them trust.
Keep an agent's work records: tasks, tracks, lessons and friction in its desk, plus Hosted Desk accounts.
Place an agent across machines and channels: rosters and failover, voice calls, and its iMessage host.
Run and administer Shepherd, which keeps an agent's coding sessions: chat, status, pauses and mandates.
Run an agent's RSVP habit: check it, move it off the legacy sender, refresh and send its report.
Change a domain's DNS records and certificate from a binding file, safely: back up, plan, apply, verify, roll back.
Schedule, test and look back at the recurring jobs an agent runs on its own, and wake it early.
Start an agent's daemon, worker or sense process directly with node, as ouro up does, mostly to debug one.
Run the Sanctuary host's root jobs: the Telegram authority, its lifecycle steps, host supervisor and health probes.
Inspect, audit, evaluate or repair saved sessions, nerves events and evaluation suites offline, outside the daemon.
